slides.title: Why does Assab matter?
slides.body: The port at the center of Ethiopia–Eritrea tensions

slides.title: Ethiopia has no coast
slides.body: It became landlocked when Eritrea became independent in 1993. PM Abiy Ahmed has repeatedly called for Red Sea access, Al Jazeera reports.

slides.title: Near a global chokepoint
slides.body: Assab, in Eritrea, sits near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the shipping lane between the Indian Ocean and the Suez Canal.

slides.title: Eritrea's position
slides.body: In an Oct 14 note to the UN Security Council, Eritrea said Ethiopia plans to seize Assab by force, calling it a “declaration of war.” As of Oct 15, Ethiopia had not publicly replied to the note.

slides.title: What analysts warn
slides.body: One scenario is a war between the two states over the border and Assab, likely drawing in regional and Gulf states. The US has urged de-escalation.

slides.title: Sea access through talks, not war.
slides.body: Follow for sourced updates from across Ethiopia.
